correctness.rationale: The defining density is nonnegative exactly for -1<=alpha<=1 and integrates to one. Its rational Laplace transform has cubic discriminant 432 alpha^2(alpha^2-1), giving exactly one real root and an explicit bound on the conjugate real parts. The Frullani identity yields the exact residual kernel after Gamma(2,2/beta) extraction. For positive alpha it splits into two nonnegative exponent differences; for negative alpha it is bounded below by exp(-t)-exp(-2t)>0. Degenerate endpoints are factored exactly. The kernel is integrable iff alpha>-1; its mass is log(4/(1+alpha)). Poisson marking yields positive integer jump intensities at every n. A standalone exact symbolic checker verified the rational identity and example; it is supplementary, not a substitute for global inequalities.

value.rationale: The natural model-building question is whether the 2023 overdispersed count family can be generated as an independent negative-binomial baseline plus genuine Poisson bursts. The theorem explicitly constructs that decomposition throughout the entire admissible signed-transmutation range, proves the all-parameter positivity obstruction, derives the exact latent finite jump rate, and identifies the sharp infinite-activity endpoint. A mixed-Poisson law alone does not imply an explicit Gamma(2,2/beta) factor. This permits aggregation and constructive sampling of the original model and is not a routine moment calculation or unmotivated narrow parameter slice.
